verses.original: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב הִנֵּ֨ה הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ בֹּכֶ֛ה וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֖ל עַל־ אַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yug·gaḏ lə·yō·w·’āḇ hin·nêh ham·me·leḵ bō·ḵeh way·yiṯ·’ab·bêl ‘al- ’aḇ·šā·lōm
verses.literal: Then it was reported to Joab . . . The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom
verses.literalPt: Foi dito a Joabe: Eis que o rei chora e lamenta a Absalão.

verses.original: וַתְּהִ֨י הַתְּשֻׁעָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא לְאֵ֖בֶל לְכָל־ הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נֶעֱצַ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ בְּנֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tə·hî hat·tə·šu·‘āh bay·yō·wm ha·hū lə·’ê·ḇel lə·ḵāl hā·‘ām kî- šā·ma‘ hā·‘ām bay·yō·wm ha·hū lê·mōr ne·‘ĕ·ṣaḇ ham·me·leḵ ‘al- bə·nōw
verses.literal: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people because on that . . . day they were told The king is grieving over his son
verses.literalPt: E a vitória converteu-se em luto, naquele dia, para todo o povo, porque o povo ouviu dizer naquele dia: O rei faz lamentações por seu filho.

verses.original: וַיִּתְגַּנֵּ֥ב הָעָ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לָב֣וֹא הָעִ֑יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְגַּנֵּ֗ב הָעָם֙ הַנִּכְלָמִ֔ים בְּנוּסָ֖ם בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiṯ·gan·nêḇ hā·‘ām bay·yō·wm ha·hū lā·ḇō·w hā·‘îr ka·’ă·šer yiṯ·gan·nêḇ hā·‘ām han·niḵ·lā·mîm bə·nū·sām bam·mil·ḥā·māh
verses.literal: So they returned to the city quietly that day as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle
verses.literalPt: Entrou o povo, naquele dia, na cidade às furtadelas, como o faz quando foge envergonhado da batalha.

verses.original: וְהַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לָאַ֣ט אֶת־ פָּנָ֔יו וַיִּזְעַ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל בְּנִי֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·ham·me·leḵ lā·’aṭ ’eṯ- pā·nāw way·yiz·‘aq ham·me·leḵ qō·wl gā·ḏō·wl bə·nî ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm bə·nî ḇə·nî
verses.literal: But the king covered his face and cried out . . . at the top of his voice O my son Absalom O Absalom my son my son
verses.literalPt: O rei, tendo coberto o rosto, clamava em alta voz: Meu filho Absalão! Absalão, filho meu, filho meu!

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֛ב אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַבָּ֑יִת וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הֹבַ֨שְׁתָּ הַיּ֜וֹם אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽמְמַלְּטִ֤ים אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֵ֨ת נֶ֤פֶשׁ בָּנֶ֙יךָ֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ נָשֶׁ֔יךָ וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ פִּלַגְשֶֽׁיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō yō·w·’āḇ ’el- ham·me·leḵ hab·bā·yiṯ way·yō·mer hō·ḇaš·tā hay·yō·wm ’eṯ- pə·nê ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏe·ḵā ham·mal·lə·ṭîm ’eṯ- nap̄·šə·ḵā hay·yō·wm wə·’êṯ ne·p̄eš bā·ne·ḵā ū·ḇə·nō·ṯe·ḵā wə·ne·p̄eš nā·še·ḵā wə·ne·p̄eš pi·laḡ·še·ḵā
verses.literal: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king Today you have disgraced - all your servants who have saved your life . . . and the lives of your sons and daughters . . . of your wives . . . and of your concubines
verses.literalPt: Joabe entrou ao rei, em casa, e disse: Cobriste hoje de confusão o rosto de todos os teus servos que hoje salvaram a tua vida, e a vida de teus filhos e filhas, e a de tuas mulheres e concubinas,

verses.original: לְאַֽהֲבָה֙ אֶת־ שֹׂ֣נְאֶ֔יךָ וְלִשְׂנֹ֖א אֶת־ אֹהֲבֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י׀ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לְךָ֙ שָׂרִ֣ים וַעֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֣י׀ יָדַ֣עְתִּי הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֠י לֹא אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם חַי֙ וְכֻלָּ֤נוּ הַיּוֹם֙ מֵתִ֔ים כִּי־ אָ֖ז יָשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: lə·’a·hă·ḇāh ’eṯ- śō·nə·’e·ḵā wə·liś·nō ’eṯ- ’ō·hă·ḇe·ḵā kî hig·gaḏ·tā hay·yō·wm kî ’ên lə·ḵā śā·rîm wa·‘ă·ḇā·ḏîm kî yā·ḏa‘·tî hay·yō·wm kî lō ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ḥay wə·ḵul·lā·nū hay·yō·wm mê·ṯîm kî- ’āz yā·šār bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā
verses.literal: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you I know today . . . that if Absalom were alive and all . . . of us were dead . . . . . . it would have pleased you . . .
verses.literalPt: amando aos que te aborrecem e aborrecendo aos que te amam. Hoje, declaraste que não se te dá nem de príncipes nem de servos, pois conheço agora que, se Absalão vivesse, e todos nós fôssemos mortos, tu ficarias muito contente.

verses.original: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם צֵ֔א וְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל־ לֵ֣ב עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ כִּי֩ בַיהוָ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי כִּי־ אֵינְךָ֣ יוֹצֵ֗א אִם־ יָלִ֨ין אִ֤ישׁ אִתְּךָ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְרָעָ֧ה לְךָ֣ זֹ֗את מִכָּל־ הָרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣אָה עָלֶ֔יךָ מִנְּעֻרֶ֖יךָ עַד־ עָֽתָּה׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·‘at·tāh qūm ṣê wə·ḏab·bêr ‘al- lêḇ ‘ă·ḇā·ḏe·ḵā kî Yah·weh niš·ba‘·tî kî- ’ê·nə·ḵā yō·w·ṣê ’im- yā·lîn ’îš ’it·tə·ḵā hal·lay·lāh wə·rā·‘āh lə·ḵā zōṯ mik·kāl hā·rā·‘āh ’ă·šer- bā·’āh ‘ā·le·ḵā min·nə·‘u·re·ḵā ‘aḏ- ‘āt·tāh
verses.literal: Now therefore get up Go out and speak . . . comfort to your servants for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out not a man will remain with you tonight This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now
verses.literalPt: Levanta-te sem demora, sai e fala palavras de conforto aos teus servos. Juro por Jeová que, se não saíres, nem sequer um homem ficará contigo esta noite; e isso será pior do que todos os males que têm vindo sobre ti desde a tua mocidade até agora.

verses.original: וַיָּ֥קָם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בַּשָּׁ֑עַר וּֽלְכָל־ הָעָ֞ם הִגִּ֣ידוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֤ה הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיָּבֹ֤א כָל־ הָעָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖ס אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yā·qām ham·me·leḵ way·yê·šeḇ baš·šā·‘ar ū·lə·ḵāl- hā·‘ām hig·gî·ḏū lê·mōr hin·nêh ham·me·leḵ yō·wō·šêḇ baš·ša·‘ar way·yā·ḇō ḵāl hā·‘ām lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ wə·yiś·rā·’êl nās ’îš lə·’ō·hā·lāw
verses.literal: So the king got up and sat in the gate and all the people were told . . . Behold the king is sitting in the gate So they all came before the king Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled each man to his home
verses.literalPt: O rei levantou-se e assentou-se à porta; e todo o povo veio apresentar-se perante o rei. Ora, Israel havia fugido, cada um para a sua tenda.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֤י כָל־ הָעָם֙ נָד֔וֹן בְּכָל־ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הִצִּילָ֣נוּ׀ מִכַּ֣ף אֹיְבֵ֗ינוּ וְה֤וּא מִלְּטָ֙נוּ֙ מִכַּ֣ף פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַתָּ֛ה בָּרַ֥ח מִן־ הָאָ֖רֶץ מֵעַ֥ל אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ḵāl hā·‘ām nā·ḏō·wn bə·ḵāl šiḇ·ṭê yiś·rā·’êl lê·mōr ham·me·leḵ hiṣ·ṣî·lā·nū mik·kap̄ ’ō·yə·ḇê·nū wə·hū mil·lə·ṭā·nū mik·kap̄ pə·liš·tîm wə·‘at·tāh bā·raḥ min- hā·’ā·reṣ mê·‘al ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines but now he has fled . . . the land because of Absalom
verses.literalPt: Todo o povo, em todas as tribos de Israel, queixava-se, dizendo: O rei livrou-nos da mão dos nossos inimigos, ele nos salvou das mãos dos filisteus e agora saiu da terra fugindo de Absalão.

verses.original: וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָשַׁ֣חְנוּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ מֵ֖ת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה לָמָ֥ה אַתֶּ֛ם מַחֲרִשִׁ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’ă·šer mā·šaḥ·nū ‘ā·lê·nū mêṯ bam·mil·ḥā·māh wə·‘at·tāh lā·māh ’at·tem ma·ḥă·ri·šîm lə·hā·šîḇ ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: But Absalom the man we anointed over us has died in battle So why do you say nothing about restoring the king
verses.literalPt: Absalão, a quem ungimos sobre nós, morreu na batalha. Agora, por que não tratais vós de fazer voltar o rei?

verses.original: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד שָׁ֠לַח אֶל־ צָד֨וֹק וְאֶל־ אֶבְיָתָ֥ר הַכֹּהֲנִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ דַּבְּר֞וּ אֶל־ זִקְנֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיוּ֙ אַֽחֲרֹנִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וּדְבַר֙ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֥א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ham·me·leḵ dā·wiḏ šā·laḥ ’el- ṣā·ḏō·wq wə·’el- ’eḇ·yā·ṯār hak·kō·hă·nîm lê·mōr dab·bə·rū ’el- ziq·nê yə·hū·ḏāh lê·mōr lām·māh ṯih·yū ’a·ḥă·rō·nîm lə·hā·šîḇ ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ ’el- bê·ṯōw ū·ḏə·ḇar kāl- yiś·rā·’êl bā ’el- ham·me·leḵ ’el- bê·ṯōw
verses.literal: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests . . . Say to the elders of Judah . . . Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace since the talk of all Israel has reached the king . . . at his quarters
verses.literalPt: O rei Davi mandou dizer aos sacerdotes Zadoque e Abiatar: Falai aos anciãos de Judá: Por que sois vós os últimos em fazer voltar o rei para a sua casa? Pois já a palavra de todo o Israel é chegada ao rei, no sentido de o trazer para sua casa.

verses.original: אַחַ֣י אַתֶּ֔ם עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אַתֶּ֑ם וְלָ֧מָּה תִהְי֛וּ אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: ’a·ḥay ’at·tem ‘aṣ·mî ū·ḇə·śā·rî ’at·tem wə·lām·māh ṯih·yū ’a·ḥă·rō·nîm lə·hā·šîḇ ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: You are my brothers my own flesh and blood So why should you be the last to restore the king
verses.literalPt: Vós sois meus irmãos, sois meu osso e minha carne; por que, então, sois vós os últimos em fazer voltar o rei?

verses.original: וְלַֽעֲמָשָׂא֙ תֹּֽמְר֔וּ הֲל֛וֹא עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף אִם־ לֹ֠א שַׂר־ צָבָ֞א תִּהְיֶ֧ה לְפָנַ֛י כָּל־ הַיָּמִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָֽב׃
verses.transliteration: wə·la·‘ă·mā·śā tō·mə·rū hă·lō·w ‘aṣ·mî ū·ḇə·śā·rî ’āt·tāh kōh ya·‘ă·śeh- lî ’ĕ·lō·hîm wə·ḵōh yō·w·sîp̄ ’im- lō śar- ṣā·ḇā tih·yeh lə·p̄ā·nay kāl- hay·yā·mîm ta·ḥaṯ yō·w·’āḇ
verses.literal: And say to Amasa Aren’t you my flesh and blood May God punish . . . me and ever so severely if from now on . . . you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab
verses.literalPt: Dizei a Amasa: Não és tu meu osso e minha carne? Assim me faça Deus e ainda mais, se não fores diante de mim para sempre general do exército, em lugar de Joabe.

verses.original: וַיַּ֛ט אֶת־ לְבַ֥ב כָּל־ אִישׁ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שׁ֥וּב אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל־ עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yaṭ ’eṯ- lə·ḇaḇ kāl- ’îš- yə·hū·ḏāh kə·’îš ’e·ḥāḏ way·yiš·lə·ḥū ’el- ham·me·leḵ šūḇ ’at·tāh wə·ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏe·ḵā
verses.literal: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man and they sent word to the king Return you and all your servants
verses.literalPt: Então, moveu ele o coração de todos os homens de Judá como se fora um só homem, de modo que enviaram a dizer ao rei: Volta com todos os teus servos.

verses.original: וַיָּ֣שָׁב הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וִיהוּדָ֞ה בָּ֣א הַגִּלְגָּ֗לָה לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַעֲבִ֥יר אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·šāḇ ham·me·leḵ way·yā·ḇō ‘aḏ- hay·yar·dên wî·hū·ḏāh bā hag·gil·gā·lāh lā·le·ḵeṯ liq·raṯ ham·me·leḵ lə·ha·‘ă·ḇîr ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên
verses.literal: So the king returned and when he arrived at the Jordan the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan
verses.literalPt: Voltou o rei e chegou ao Jordão. Judá foi a Gilgal para receber o rei, a fim de fazê-lo passar o Jordão.

verses.original: וַיְמַהֵ֗ר שִׁמְעִ֤י בֶן־ גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן־ הַיְמִינִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֙רֶד֙ עִם־ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽד׃
verses.transliteration: way·ma·hêr šim·‘î ḇen- gê·rā ben- hay·mî·nî ’ă·šer mib·ba·ḥū·rîm way·yê·reḏ ‘im- ’îš yə·hū·ḏāh liq·raṯ ham·me·leḵ dā·wiḏ
verses.literal: Then Shimei son of Gera a Benjamite from Bahurim . . . hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David
verses.literalPt: Apressou-se Simei, filho de Gera, benjamita, que era de Baurim, e desceu com os homens de Judá a encontrar-se com o rei Davi.

verses.original: וְאֶ֨לֶף אִ֣ישׁ עִמּוֹ֮ מִבִּנְיָמִן֒ וְצִיבָ֗א נַ֚עַר בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וַחֲמֵ֨שֶׁת עָשָׂ֥ר בָּנָ֛יו וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וְצָלְח֥וּ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’e·lep̄ ’îš ‘im·mōw mib·bin·yā·min wə·ṣî·ḇā na·‘ar bêṯ šā·’ūl wa·ḥă·mê·šeṯ ‘ā·śār bā·nāw wə·‘eś·rîm ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw ’it·tōw wə·ṣā·lə·ḥū hay·yar·dên lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: along with a thousand men of Benjamin as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen . . . sons and twenty servants They rushed down to the Jordan before the king
verses.literalPt: Com ele estavam mil homens de Benjamim e Ziba, servo da casa de Saul, acompanhado de seus quinze filhos e dos seus vinte servos. Meteram-se pelo Jordão adiante do rei,

verses.original: וְעָבְרָ֣ה הָעֲבָרָ֗ה לַֽעֲבִיר֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינוֹ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן־ גֵּרָ֗א נָפַל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּעָבְר֖וֹ בַּיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
verses.transliteration: wə·‘ā·ḇə·rāh hā·‘ă·ḇā·rāh la·‘ă·ḇîr ’eṯ- bêṯ ham·me·leḵ wə·la·‘ă·śō·wṯ haṭ·ṭō·wḇ bə·ʿē·nō wə·šim·‘î ḇen- gê·rā nā·p̄al lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ bə·‘ā·ḇə·rōw bay·yar·dên
verses.literal: and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan he fell down before the king
verses.literalPt: passando repetidas vezes o vau, para conduzirem os da casa real e para fazerem o que lhe era agradável. Simei prostrou-se perante o rei, quando havia passado o Jordão,

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אַל־ יַחֲשָׁב־ לִ֣י אֲדֹנִי֮ עָוֺן֒ וְאַל־ תִּזְכֹּ֗ר אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱוָ֣ה עַבְדְּךָ֔ בַּיּ֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יָׄצָ֥ׄאׄ אֲדֹנִֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לָשׂ֥וּם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ לִבּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’el- ham·me·leḵ ’al- ya·ḥă·šāḇ- lî ’ă·ḏō·nî ‘ā·wōn wə·’al- tiz·kōr ’êṯ ’ă·šer he·‘ĕ·wāh ‘aḇ·də·ḵā bay·yō·wm ’ă·šer- yå̄·ṣå̄ ’ă·ḏō·nî- ham·me·leḵ mî·rū·šā·lim lā·śūm ham·me·leḵ ’el- lib·bōw
verses.literal: and said - My lord do not hold me guilty and do not remember - your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem May the king not take it to heart
verses.literalPt: e disse-lhe: Não me tenhas por culpado, meu senhor, nem te lembres do que, perversamente, fez o teu servo no dia em que o rei, meu senhor, saiu de Jerusalém, para levá-lo em conta.

verses.original: כִּ֚י יָדַ֣ע עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י חָטָ֑אתִי וְהִנֵּֽה־ בָ֣אתִי הַיּ֗וֹם רִאשׁוֹן֙ לְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לָרֶ֕דֶת לִקְרַ֖את אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
verses.transliteration: kî yā·ḏa‘ ‘aḇ·də·ḵā kî ’ă·nî ḥā·ṭā·ṯî wə·hin·nêh- ḇā·ṯî hay·yō·wm ri·šō·wn lə·ḵāl bêṯ yō·w·sêp̄ lā·re·ḏeṯ liq·raṯ ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: For your servant knows that I have sinned so here I am . . . today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king
verses.literalPt: Pois eu, teu servo, conheço que pequei; por isso, sou vindo hoje o primeiro de toda a casa de José para descer ao encontro do rei, meu senhor.

verses.original: וַיַּ֨עַן אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הֲתַ֣חַת זֹ֔את לֹ֥א יוּמַ֖ת שִׁמְעִ֑י כִּ֥י קִלֵּ֖ל אֶת־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an ’ă·ḇî·šay ben- ṣə·rū·yāh way·yō·mer hă·ṯa·ḥaṯ zōṯ lō yū·maṯ šim·‘î kî qil·lêl ’eṯ- mə·šî·aḥ Yah·weh
verses.literal: But Abishai son of Zeruiah . . . said Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this because he cursed the LORD’s anointed
verses.literalPt: Abisai, porém, filho de Zeruia, respondeu e disse: Não será morto Simei, por ter amaldiçoado o ungido de Jeová?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד מַה־ לִּ֤י וְלָכֶם֙ בְּנֵ֣י צְרוּיָ֔ה כִּי־ תִֽהְיוּ־ לִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם לְשָׂטָ֑ן הַיּ֗וֹם י֤וּמַת אִישׁ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֚י הֲל֣וֹא יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֲנִי־ מֶ֥לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ mah- lî wə·lā·ḵem bə·nê ṣə·rū·yāh kî- ṯih·yū- lî hay·yō·wm lə·śā·ṭān hay·yō·wm yū·maṯ ’îš bə·yiś·rā·’êl kî hă·lō·w yā·ḏa‘·tî kî hay·yō·wm ’ă·nî- me·leḵ ‘al- yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: And David replied Sons of Zeruiah what have I to do with you that you should be my adversaries today Should any man be put to death in Israel today Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel
verses.literalPt: Davi disse: Que tenho eu convosco, filhos de Zeruia, para que hoje me sejais adversários? Há de hoje tirar-se a vida a alguém em Israel? Pois não sei eu que hoje sou feito rei em Israel?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ שִׁמְעִ֖י לֹ֣א תָמ֑וּת וַיִּשָּׁ֥בַֽע ל֖וֹ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- šim·‘î lō ṯā·mūṯ way·yiš·šā·ḇa‘ lōw ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: So the king said to Shimei You shall not die And the king swore an oath to him
verses.literalPt: Então, disse o rei a Simei: Não morrerás. O rei lho jurou.

verses.original: וּמְפִבֹ֙שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־ שָׁא֔וּל יָרַ֖ד לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹא־ עָשָׂ֨ה רַגְלָ֜יו וְלֹא־ עָשָׂ֣ה שְׂפָמ֗וֹ וְאֶת־ בְּגָדָיו֙ לֹ֣א כִבֵּ֔ס לְמִן־ הַיּוֹם֙ לֶ֣כֶת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד־ הַיּ֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: ū·mə·p̄i·ḇō·šeṯ ben- šā·’ūl yā·raḏ liq·raṯ ham·me·leḵ wə·lō- ‘ā·śāh raḡ·lāw wə·lō- ‘ā·śāh śə·p̄ā·mōw wə·’eṯ- bə·ḡā·ḏāw lō ḵib·bês lə·min- hay·yō·wm le·ḵeṯ ham·me·leḵ ‘aḏ- hay·yō·wm ’ă·šer- bā ḇə·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: Then Mephibosheth Saul’s grandson went down to meet the king He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes . . . from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely
verses.literalPt: Desceu também Mefibosete, filho de Saul, a receber o rei; ele não dera cuidado aos pés, nem tinha feito a barba, nem lavado os vestidos desde o dia em que o rei saíra até o dia em que voltou em paz.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֛י כִּי־ בָ֥א יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֛מָּה לֹא־ הָלַ֥כְתָּ עִמִּ֖י מְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kî- ḇā yə·rū·šā·lim liq·raṯ ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mer lōw ham·me·leḵ lām·māh lō- hā·laḵ·tā ‘im·mî mə·p̄î·ḇō·šeṯ
verses.literal: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king who asked him Mephibosheth why did you not go with me
verses.literalPt: Tendo chegado a Jerusalém para se encontrar com o rei, perguntou-lhe este: Por que não foste comigo, Mefibosete?

verses.original: וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַבְדִּ֣י רִמָּ֑נִי כִּֽי־ אָמַ֨ר עַבְדְּךָ֜ אֶחְבְּשָׁה־ לִּי֩ הַחֲמ֨וֹר וְאֶרְכַּ֤ב עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ וְאֵלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י פִסֵּ֖חַ עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mar ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ ‘aḇ·dî rim·mā·nî kî- ’ā·mar ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’eḥ·bə·šāh- lî ha·ḥă·mō·wr wə·’er·kaḇ ‘ā·le·hā wə·’ê·lêḵ ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ kî p̄is·sê·aḥ ‘aḇ·de·ḵā
verses.literal: My lord the king he replied because I am lame I said I will have my donkey . . . saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king But my servant Ziba deceived me
verses.literalPt: Respondeu ele: Ó rei, meu senhor, o meu criado me enganou. Pois o teu servo disse: Eu albardarei um jumento, para nele montar e ir com o rei; porque o teu servo é coxo.

verses.original: וַיְרַגֵּ֣ל בְּעַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·rag·gêl bə·‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’el- ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ wa·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ kə·mal·’aḵ hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm wa·‘ă·śêh haṭ·ṭō·wḇ bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā
verses.literal: and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God so do what is good in your eyes
verses.literalPt: Mas ele, falsamente, acusou o teu servo diante do rei, meu senhor; porém tu, ó rei, meu senhor, és como um anjo de Deus. Faze, pois, o que bem te parecer.

verses.original: כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הָיָ֜ה כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֗י כִּ֤י אִם־ אַנְשֵׁי־ מָ֙וֶת֙ לַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתָּ֙שֶׁת֙ אֶֽת־ עַבְדְּךָ֔ בְּאֹכְלֵ֖י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ וּמַה־ יֶּשׁ־ לִ֥י עוֹד֙ צְדָקָ֔ה וְלִזְעֹ֥ק ע֖וֹד אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
verses.transliteration: kî lō hā·yāh kāl- bêṯ ’ā·ḇî kî ’im- ’an·šê- mā·weṯ la·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ wat·tā·šeṯ ’eṯ- ‘aḇ·də·ḵā bə·’ō·ḵə·lê šul·ḥā·ne·ḵā ū·mah- yeš- lî ‘ō·wḏ ṣə·ḏā·qāh wə·liz·‘ōq ‘ō·wḏ ’el- ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: For . . . . . . all the house of my grandfather . . . . . . . . . deserves death from my lord the king yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table What further right, then do I have . . . to keep appealing to the king
verses.literalPt: Pois toda a casa de meu pai não era senão digna de morte diante do rei, meu senhor; contudo, puseste o teu servo entre os que comem à tua mesa. Que direito mais tenho eu de clamar ainda ao rei?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֛מָּה תְּדַבֵּ֥ר ע֖וֹד דְּבָרֶ֑יךָ אָמַ֕רְתִּי אַתָּ֣ה וְצִיבָ֔א תַּחְלְק֖וּ אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lōw ham·me·leḵ lām·māh tə·ḏab·bêr ‘ō·wḏ də·ḇā·re·ḵā ’ā·mar·tî ’at·tāh wə·ṣî·ḇā taḥ·lə·qū ’eṯ- haś·śā·ḏeh
verses.literal: The king replied Why say any more I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhe o rei: Por que falas ainda dos teus negócios? Resolvo que com Ziba repartas as terras.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מְפִיבֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ גַּ֥ם אֶת־ הַכֹּ֖ל יִקָּ֑ח אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֞א אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶך בְּשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer mə·p̄î·ḇō·šeṯ ’el- ham·me·leḵ gam ’eṯ- hak·kōl yiq·qāḥ ’a·ḥă·rê ’ă·šer- bā ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·mɛ·lɛḵ bə·šā·lō·wm ’el- bê·ṯōw
verses.literal: And Mephibosheth said to the king Instead since my lord the king has safely come to his own house let Ziba take it all
verses.literalPt: Disse Mefibosete ao rei: Fique ele muito embora com tudo, uma vez que o rei, meu senhor, já voltou em paz à sua casa.

verses.original: וּבַרְזִלַּי֙ הַגִּלְעָדִ֔י יָרַ֖ד מֵרֹגְלִ֑ים וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר אֶת־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לְשַׁלְּח֖וֹ אֶת־ בַּיַּרְדֵּן׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇar·zil·lay hag·gil·‘ā·ḏî yā·raḏ mê·rō·ḡə·lîm way·ya·‘ă·ḇōr ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ hay·yar·dên lə·šal·lə·ḥōw ’eṯ- bay·yar·dēn
verses.literal: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there
verses.literalPt: Também Barzilai, gileadita, desceu de Rogelim, e passou na companhia do rei para o acompanhar até a outra banda do Jordão.

verses.original: וּבַרְזִלַּי֙ זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֔ד בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וְהֽוּא־ כִלְכַּ֤ל אֶת־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּשִׁיבָת֣וֹ בְמַחֲנַ֔יִם כִּֽי־ אִ֛ישׁ גָּד֥וֹל ה֖וּא מְאֹֽד׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇar·zil·lay zā·qên mə·’ōḏ ben- šə·mō·nîm šā·nāh wə·hū- ḵil·kal ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ ḇə·šî·ḇā·ṯōw ḇə·ma·ḥă·na·yim kî- ’îš gā·ḏō·wl hū mə·’ōḏ
verses.literal: Barzillai was quite old eighty years of age and since he was a very wealthy man . . . he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim
verses.literalPt: Era Barzilai muito velho, da idade de oitenta anos. Ele tinha provido o rei de víveres, quando estava em Maanaim, porque era um homem muito rico.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ בַּרְזִלָּ֑י אַתָּה֙ עֲבֹ֣ר אִתִּ֔י וְכִלְכַּלְתִּ֥י אֹתְךָ֛ עִמָּדִ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- bar·zil·lāy ’at·tāh ‘ă·ḇōr ’it·tî wə·ḵil·kal·tî ’ō·ṯə·ḵā ‘im·mā·ḏî bî·rū·šā·lim
verses.literal: The king said to Barzillai . . . Cross over with me and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Disse o rei a Barzilai: Passa tu comigo, e te sustentarei em Jerusalém.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר בַּרְזִלַּ֖י אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כַּמָּ֗ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י כִּי־ אֶעֱלֶ֥ה אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer bar·zil·lay ’el- ham·me·leḵ kam·māh yə·mê šə·nê ḥay·yay kî- ’e·‘ĕ·leh ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ yə·rū·šā·lim
verses.literal: But Barzillai replied - How many years . . . of my life remain that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Barzilai ao rei: Quantos são os dias dos anos da minha vida, para que eu suba com o rei a Jerusalém?

verses.original: בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָה֩ אָנֹכִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם הַאֵדַ֣ע׀ בֵּין־ ט֣וֹב לְרָ֗ע אִם־ יִטְעַ֤ם עַבְדְּךָ֙ אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֹכַל֙ וְאֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁתֶּ֔ה אִם־ אֶשְׁמַ֣ע ע֔וֹד בְּק֖וֹל שָׁרִ֣ים וְשָׁר֑וֹת וְלָמָּה֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ עוֹד֙ לְמַשָּׂ֔א אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: ben- šə·mō·nîm šā·nāh ’ā·nō·ḵî hay·yō·wm ha·’ê·ḏa‘ bên- ṭō·wḇ lə·rā‘ ’im- yiṭ·‘am ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’eṯ- ’ă·šer ’ō·ḵal wə·’eṯ- ’ă·šer ’eš·teh ’im- ’eš·ma‘ ‘ō·wḏ bə·qō·wl šā·rîm wə·šā·rō·wṯ wə·lām·māh yih·yeh ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ‘ō·wḏ lə·maś·śā ’el- ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: I am now eighty years old . . . Can I discern . . . what is good and what is not . . . Can your servant taste what he eats - or drinks . . . Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king
verses.literalPt: Oitenta anos tenho hoje; poderei eu discernir entre o bom e o mau? Poderá o teu servo perceber o sabor no que come ou no que bebe? Poderei mais ouvir a voz dos cantores ou das cantoras? Por que há de ser o teu servo ainda pesado ao rei, meu senhor?

verses.original: כִּמְעַ֞ט יַעֲבֹ֧ר עַבְדְּךָ֛ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלָ֙מָּה֙ יִגְמְלֵ֣נִי הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַגְּמוּלָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
verses.transliteration: kim·‘aṭ ya·‘ă·ḇōr ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ wə·lām·māh yiḡ·mə·lê·nî ham·me·leḵ hag·gə·mū·lāh haz·zōṯ
verses.literal: Your servant will go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan why should the king repay me with such a reward
verses.literalPt: O teu servo só quer passar o Jordão com o rei; por que há de me pagar o rei com tal recompensa?

verses.original: יָֽשָׁב־ נָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאָמֻ֣ת בְּעִירִ֔י עִ֛ם קֶ֥בֶר אָבִ֖י וְאִמִּ֑י וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ עַבְדְּךָ֣ כִמְהָ֗ם יַֽעֲבֹר֙ עִם־ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַעֲשֵׂה־ ל֕וֹ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ ט֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃ס
verses.transliteration: yā·šāḇ- nā ‘aḇ·də·ḵā wə·’ā·muṯ bə·‘î·rî ‘im qe·ḇer ’ā·ḇî wə·’im·mî wə·hin·nêh ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ḵim·hām ya·‘ă·ḇōr ‘im- ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ wa·‘ă·śêh- lōw ’êṯ ’ă·šer- ṭō·wḇ bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā
verses.literal: Please let your servant return that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother But here is your servant Chimham Let him cross over with my lord the king and do for him what is good in your sight
verses.literalPt: Deixa voltar o teu servo para que eu morra na minha cidade e seja enterrado junto à sepultura de meu pai e de minha mãe. Mas eis aqui o teu servo Quimã. Passe ele com o rei, meu senhor; e faze-lhe o que for do teu agrado.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אִתִּי֙ יַעֲבֹ֣ר כִּמְהָ֔ם וַאֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂה־ לּ֔וֹ אֶת־ הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ תִּבְחַ֥ר עָלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּֽךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’it·tî ya·‘ă·ḇōr kim·hām wa·’ă·nî ’e·‘ĕ·śeh- lōw ’eṯ- haṭ·ṭō·wḇ bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā wə·ḵōl ’ă·šer- tiḇ·ḥar ‘ā·lay ’e·‘ĕ·śeh- lāḵ
verses.literal: The king replied Chimham will cross over with me and I will do for him what is good in your sight and I will do for you whatever you desire of me
verses.literalPt: Respondeu o rei: Quimã passará comigo e far-lhe-ei o que bem te parecer. Tudo o que de mim exigires, isso te farei.

verses.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר כָּל־ הָעָ֛ם אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עָבָ֑ר וַיִּשַּׁ֨ק הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ לְבַרְזִלַּי֙ וַיְבָ֣רֲכֵ֔הוּ וַיָּ֖שָׁב לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘ă·ḇōr kāl- hā·‘ām ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên wə·ham·me·leḵ ‘ā·ḇār way·yiš·šaq ham·me·leḵ lə·ḇar·zil·lay way·ḇā·ră·ḵê·hū way·yā·šāḇ lim·qō·mōw
verses.literal: So all the people crossed the Jordan and then the king crossed over The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him and Barzillai returned home
verses.literalPt: Todo o povo passou o Jordão; também o rei passou. O rei beijou a Barzilai e o abençoou; e este voltou para o seu lugar.

verses.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֔לָה וְכִמְהָ֖ן עָבַ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ וְכָל־ עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙ וַיַּעֲבִרוּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְגַ֕ם חֲצִ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘ă·ḇōr ham·me·leḵ hag·gil·gā·lāh wə·ḵim·hān ‘ā·ḇar ‘im·mōw wə·ḵāl ‘am yə·hū·ḏāh way·ya·ʿă·ḇi·rū ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ wə·ḡam ḥă·ṣî ‘am yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: Then the king crossed over to Gilgal and Chimham crossed over with him All the troops of Judah . . . and half the troops of Israel escorted the king
verses.literalPt: Passou o rei para Gilgal, e Quimã passou em sua companhia. Todo o povo de Judá conduziu o rei, e bem assim a metade do povo de Israel.

verses.original: וְהִנֵּ֛ה כָּל־ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּאִ֣ים אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ מַדּוּעַ֩ גְּנָב֨וּךָ אַחֵ֜ינוּ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּעֲבִ֨רוּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְאֶת־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י דָוִ֖ד עִמּֽוֹ׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·hin·nêh kāl- ’îš yiś·rā·’êl bā·’îm ’el- ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mə·rū ’el- ham·me·leḵ mad·dū·a‘ gə·nā·ḇū·ḵā ’a·ḥê·nū ’îš yə·hū·ḏāh way·ya·‘ă·ḇi·rū ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ wə·’eṯ- bê·ṯōw ’eṯ- hay·yar·dên wə·ḵāl ’an·šê ḏā·wiḏ ‘im·mōw
verses.literal: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked . . . . . . Why did our brothers the men of Judah take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan together with all of David’s men
verses.literalPt: Eis que todos os homens de Israel vieram ter com o rei e lhe disseram: Por que te roubaram nossos irmãos, os homens de Judá, e fizeram ao rei, e a toda a sua casa, e a todos os homens de Davi passar o Jordão?

verses.original: וַיַּעַן֩ כָּל־ אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה עַל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּֽי־ קָר֤וֹב הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֵלַ֔י וְלָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ חָרָ֣ה לְךָ֔ עַל־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה הֶאָכ֤וֹל אָכַ֙לְנוּ֙ מִן־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־ נִשֵּׂ֥את נִשָּׂ֖א לָֽנוּ׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an kāl- ’îš yə·hū·ḏāh ‘al- ’îš yiś·rā·’êl kî- qā·rō·wḇ ham·me·leḵ ’ê·lay wə·lām·māh zeh ḥā·rāh lə·ḵā ‘al- had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh he·’ā·ḵō·wl ’ā·ḵal·nū min- ham·me·leḵ ’im- niś·śêṯ niś·śā lā·nū
verses.literal: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel We did this because the king is our relative Why does this anger you . . . . . . . . . Have we ever eaten . . . at the king’s expense or . . . received anything for ourselves
verses.literalPt: Todos os homens de Judá responderam aos homens de Israel: Porque o rei é nosso parente chegado. Por que é que vos irais por isso? Acaso, temos comido à custa do rei? Ou tem-se-nos dado algum presente?

verses.original: וַיַּ֣עַן אִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ אֶת־ אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עֶֽשֶׂר־ יָד֨וֹת לִ֣י בַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וְגַם־ בְּדָוִד֮ אֲנִ֣י מִמְּךָ֒ וּמַדּ֙וּעַ֙ הֱקִלֹּתַ֔נִי וְלֹא־ הָיָ֨ה דְבָרִ֥י רִאשׁ֛וֹן לִ֖י לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶת־ מַלְכִּ֑י וַיִּ֙קֶשׁ֙ דְּבַר־ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְּבַ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an ’îš- yiś·rā·’êl ’eṯ- ’îš yə·hū·ḏāh way·yō·mer ‘e·śer- yā·ḏō·wṯ lî ḇam·me·leḵ wə·ḡam- bə·ḏā·wiḏ ’ă·nî mim·mə·ḵā ū·mad·dū·a‘ hĕ·qil·lō·ṯa·nî wə·lō- hā·yāh ḏə·ḇā·rî ri·šō·wn lî lə·hā·šîḇ ’eṯ- mal·kî way·yi·qeš də·ḇar- ’îš yə·hū·ḏāh mid·də·ḇar ’îš yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: We have ten shares in the king answered the men of Israel - so we have more claim . . . to David than you Why then do you despise us Were we not . . . the first to speak of restoring our king But the men of Judah spoke more fiercely . . . than the men of Israel
verses.literalPt: Os homens de Israel responderam aos homens de Judá: Dez partes temos no rei, e mais nos toca também Davi a nós do que a vós; por que não fizestes caso de nós, quando fomos nós que primeiro falamos em fazer voltar o nosso rei? Porém as palavras dos homens de Judá eram mais desabridas do que as palavras dos homens de Israel.
